To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
deep learning can be used to estimate the real and apparent age from a single face without the need for facial landmarks.

(1) deep learning models can estimate real age from a face image with a high accuracy of 5.4 years, and (2) the same model with the same training data can be applied to the task of apparent age estimation, achieving 5.2 years of accuracy, which is the state of the art.
we propose a new dataset, IMDB-WIKA, and introduce a novel approach for age estimation using deep learning that is based on a deep classification followed by a regression refinement.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: 1) How can we estimate a person’s real age from a face image? 2) How can we predict a person’s apparent age from the same image? 3) How can we train a CNN to solve these problems?
